transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m glad you clarified that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Hankins, I don’t feel good about it, and I think we ought to have a patient’s bill of rights to take the medical decisions away from the HMOs and give them back to the doctors and nurses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to come back and tell you why, but if you will forgive me, I would like to say something right now at the beginning of this debate following on the moment of silence for Mel Carnahan and Randy Carnahan and Chris Sifford.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Tipper and I were good friends with Mel and Randy, and I know that all of us here want to extend our sympathy and condolences to Jean and the family and to the Sifford family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I would just like to say that this debate in a way is a living tribute to Mel Carnahan because he loved the vigorous discussion of ideas in our democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: He was a fantastic governor of Missouri.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: This state became one of the top five in the nation for health care coverage for children under his leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: One of the best in advancing all kinds of benefits for children to grow up healthy and strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And of course, this debate also takes place at a time when the tragedy of the USS Cole is on our minds and hearts and insofar as the memorial service is tomorrow, I would like to also extend sympathy to the families of those who have died and those who are still missing, and the injured.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Hankins, I think that the situation that you describe has gotten completely out of hand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Doctors are giving prescriptions, they’re recommending treatments, and then their recommendations are being overruled by HMOs and insurance companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That is unacceptable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I support a strong national patient’s bill of rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It is actually a disagreement between us, a national law that is pending on this, the Dingle-Norwood bill, a bipartisan bill, is one that I support and that the governor does not.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I, too, want to extend my prayers and blessings, God’s blessings on the families whose lives were overturned yes — tod — last night.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a tragic moment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Actually, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President, it’s not true.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do support a national patient’s bill of rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, I brought Republicans and Democrats together to do just that in the State of Texas to get a patient’s bill of rights through.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It requires a different kind of leadership style to do it, though.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You see, in order to get something done on behalf of the people, you have to put partisanship aside, and that’s what we did in my state.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have one of the most advanced patient’s bill of rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It says, for example, that a woman doesn’t have to go through a gate keeper to go to her gynecologist.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It says that you can’t gag a doctor, doctor can advise you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The HMO, the insurance company, can’t gag that doctor from giving you full advice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And this particular bill, it allows patients to choose a doctor, their own doctor if they want to.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we did something else that was interesting.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re one of the first states that said you can sue an HMO for denying you proper coverage.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now there’s what’s called an Independent Review Organization that you have to go through first.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It says if youâ€™ve got a complaint with your insurance company, you can take your complaint to an objective body.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If the objective body rules on your behalf, the insurance company must follow those rules.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: However, if the insurance company doesn’t follow the findings of the IRO, then that becomes a cause of action in a court of law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time for our nation to come together and do what’s right for the people, and I think this is right for the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, I support a national patient’s bill of rights, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President, and I want all people covered.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want the law to supersede good law like we’ve got in Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think —

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Jim, we have a direct disagreement on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I referred to the Dingle-Norwood bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It is the bipartisan bill that is now pending in the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The HMOs and the insurance companies support the other bill that’s pending, the one that the Republican majority has put forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They like it because it doesn’t accomplish what I think really needs to be accomplished to give the decisions back to the doctors and nurses and give you a right of appeal to somebody other than the HMO or insurance company, let you go to the nearest emergency room without having to call an HMO before you call 911, to let you see a specialist if you need to, and it has strong bipartisan support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It is being blocked by the Republican leadership in the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I specifically would like to know whether Governor Bush will support the Dingle-Norwood bill, which is the main one pending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, the difference is is that I can get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That I can get something positive done on behalf of the people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what the question in this campaign is about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not only what’s your philosophy and what’s your position on issues, but can you get things done?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I believe I can.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: What about the Dingle-Norwood bill?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m not quite through.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me finish.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I talked about the principles and the issues that I think are important in a patient’s bill of rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s kind of Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: focus.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, it’s in this committee or it’s got this sponsor.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If I’m the president, we’re going to have emergency room care, we’re going have gag orders, we’re going to have direct access to OB/GYN.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: People will be able to take their HMO insurance company to court.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what I’ve done in Texas and that’s the kind of leadership style I’ll bring to Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, that’s a great question.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think one of the problems we have, particularly for seniors, is there is no prescription drug coverage in Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And therefore, when they have to try to purchase drugs they do so on their own, there’s no kind of collective bargaining, no power of purchasing among seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I think step one to make sure prescription drugs is more affordable for seniors, and those are the folks who really rely upon prescription drugs a lot these days, is to reform the Medicare system, is to have prescription drugs as an integral part of Medicare once and for all.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The problem we have today is like the patient’s bill of rights, particularly with health care, there’s a lot of bickering in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s kind of like a political issue as opposed to a people issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So what I want to do is I want to call upon Republicans and Democrats to forget all the arguing and finger pointing, and come together and take care of our seniors’ prescription drug program, that says we’ll pay for the poor seniors, we’ll help all seniors with prescription drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In the meantime, I think it’s important to have what’s called Immediate Helping Hand, which is direct money to states so that seniors, poor seniors, don’t have to choose between food and medicine.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s part of an overall overhaul.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The purchasing powers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m against price controls.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think price controls would hurt our ability to continue important research and development.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Drug therapies are replacing a lot of medicines as we used to know it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One of the most important things is to continue the research and development component.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I’m against price controls.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Expediting drugs through the FDA makes sense, of course.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Allowing the new bill that was passed in the Congress made sense to allow for, you know, drugs that were sold overseas to come back and other countries to come back into the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That makes sense.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the best thing to do is to reform Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: All right, here we go again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now look, if you want someone who will spend a lot of words describing a whole convoluted process and then end up supporting legislation that is supported by the big drug companies, this is your man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you want someone who will fight for you and who will fight for the middle-class families and working men and women, who are sick and tired of having their parents and grandparents pay higher prices for prescription drugs than anybody else, then I want to fight for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And you asked a great question because it’s not only seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Listen, for 24 years I have never been afraid to take on the big drug companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They do some great things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They discover great new cures and that’s great.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We want them to continue that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But they are now spending more money on advertising and promotion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You see all these ads?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Than they are on research and development.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And they are trying artificially extend the monopoly patent protection so they can keep charging these very high prices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to streamline the approval of the competing generic drugs and the new kinds of treatments that can compete with them so we bring the price down for everybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, briefly, let me tell you how my prescription drug plan works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The governor talked about Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I propose a real prescription drug benefit under Medicare for all seniors, all seniors, and here’s how it works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You pick your own doctor, and nobody can take that away from you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The doctor chooses the prescription that you need and nobody can overrule your doctor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You go to your own pharmacy and then Medicare pays half the price.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you’re poor, they pay all of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you have extraordinarily high cost, then they pay all over $4,000 out-of-pocket.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll bring new competition to bring the price down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And if you pass the big drug companies’ bill, nothing will happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that we should move step-by-step toward universal health coverage, but I am not in favor of government doing it all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We’ve spent 65 years now on the development of a hybrid system, partly private, partly public, and 85% of our people have health insurance, 15% don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That adds up to 44 million people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That is a national outrage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have got to get health coverage for those who do not have it and we’ve got to improve the quality for those who do with a patient’s bill of rights that’s real and that works, the Dingle-Norwood bill, and we have got to fill in the gaps in coverage by finally bringing parity for the treatment of mental illness, because that’s been left out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have got to deal with long-term care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, here are the steps that I would take, first of all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will make a commitment to bring health care coverage of high quality that is affordable to every single child in America within four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And then we’ll fill other gaps by covering the parents of those children when the family is poor or up to two and a half times the poverty rate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to give a tax credit for the purchase of individual health insurance plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to give small business employers a tax credit, 25%, to encourage the providing of health insurance for the employees in small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to give seniors who are, well, the near elderly, I don’t like that term because I am just about in that category, but those 55 to 65 ought to be able to buy into Medicare for premiums that are reasonable and fair and significantly below what they have to get now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, we have a big difference on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And you need to know the record here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Under Governor Bush, Texas has sunk to be 50th out of 50 in health care — in health insurance for their citizens.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Last week he said that they were spending 3.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: 7 billion dollars, or 4.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: 7 billion dollars on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Okay.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m absolutely opposed to a national health care plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want the federal government making decisions for consumers or for providers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I remember what the administration tried to do in 1993.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They tried to have a national health care plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And fortunately, it failed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I trust people, I don’t trust the federal government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to be one of the themes you hear tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want the federal government making decisions on behalf of everybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is an issue with the uninsured, there sure is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we have uninsured people in my state.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Ours is a big state, a fast-growing state.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We share a common border with another nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we’re providing health care for our people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One thing about insurance, that’s a Washington term.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The question is, are people getting health care, and we have a strong safety net, and there needs to be a safety net in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There needs to be more community health clinics where the poor can go get health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need a program for the uninsured.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’ve been talking about it in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The number of uninsured has now gone up for the past seven years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need a $2,000 credit, rebate for people, working people that don’t have insurance, they can get in the marketplace and start purchasing insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to have — allow small businesses to write insurance across jurisdictional lines so small business can afford health care, small restaurants can afford health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So health care needs to be affordable and available.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have to trust people to make decisions with their lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In the Medicare reform I talk about it says if you are a senior, you can stay in Medicare if you like it, and that’s fine, but we’re going to give you other choices to choose if you want to do so, just like they do the federal employees.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The people that work in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: for the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Congress or the United States senate.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Get a variety of choices to make in their lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what we ought to do for all people in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Follow-up?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Trying to find my light.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, you know, it’s hard to make people love one another.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I wish I knew the law because I would darn sure sign it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I wish I knew the law that said all of us would be good parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One of the things the next president must do is to remind people that if we are going to have a responsible period in America, that each of us must love our children with all our heart and all our soul.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I happened to believe strong accountability encourages parental involvement, though.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think when you measure and post results on the Internet or in the town newspapers, most parents say wait a minute, my child’s school isn’t doing what I want it to do and, therefore, become involved in education.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I recognize there are some who just don’t seem to care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But there are a lot of parents who feel like everything is going well in their child’s school, and all of a sudden they wake up and realize that wait a minute, standards aren’t being met.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I’m so strong for accountability.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe we ought to measure a lot, three, four, five, six, seven, eighth grade.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We do so in my state of Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One of the good things we’ve gone in Texas is we have strong accountability because you can’t cure unless you know.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t solve a problem unless you diagnose it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I strongly believe that one of the best things to encourage parental involvement also is to know that the classrooms will be safe and secure.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I support a teacher liability act at the federal level, that says if a teacher or principal upholds reasonable standards of classroom discipline they can’t be sued.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They can’t be sued.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think parents will be more involved with education when they know their children’s classrooms are safe and secure as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I also believe that we need to say to people that if you cannot meet standards, there has to be a consequence.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Instead of just comes the soft bigotry of low expectations, that there has to be a consequence.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can’t continue to shuffle children through school.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And one of the consequences to allow parents to have different choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have huge difference between us on this question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to start by telling you what my vision is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I see a day in the United States of America where all of our public schools are considered excellent, world class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Where there are no failing schools, where the classrooms are small enough in size, number of students, so that the teacher can spend enough one-on-one time with each student.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now that means recruiting new teachers for the public schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It means in my plan hiring bonuses to get 100,000 new teachers in the public schools within the next four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It means also helping local school districts that sometimes find the parents of school age children outvoted on bond issues, to give them some help with interest-free bonding authority so that we can build new schools and modernize the classrooms.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We need to give teachers the training and professional development that they need, including a paid time off to go visit the classroom of a master teacher to pick up some new skills.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to give every middle-class family a $10,000 a year tax deduction for college tuition so that middle-class families will always be able to send their kids on to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to work for universal free school because we know from all the studies that the youngsters learn, kids learn more in the first few years of life than any where else.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, I said there was a contrast.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Governor Bush is for vouchers, and in his plan he proposes to drain more money, more taxpayer money out of the public schools for private school vouchers than all of the money that he proposes in his entire budget for public schools themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And only one in 20 students would be eligible for these vouchers, and they wouldn’t even pay the full tuition to private school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that’s a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we should give up on the private schools and leave kids trapped in failing schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think we — I think we should make it the number one priority to make our schools the best in the world, all of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, I appreciate that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think any time we end with one of these attacks, it’s appropriate to respond.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Here’s what I think.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First of all, vouchers are up to states.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you want to do a voucher program in Missouri, fine.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I strongly believe in local control of schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m a governor of state and I don’t like it when the federal government tells us what to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe in local control of schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But here’s what I said.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve said to the extent we spend federal money on disadvantaged children, we want the schools to show us whether or not the children are learning.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What’s unreasonable about that?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We expect there to be standards met and we expect there to be measurement.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if we find success we’ll praise it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But when we find children trapped in schools that will not change and will not teach, instead of saying oh, this is okay in America just to shuffle poor kids through schools, there has to be a consequence.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the consequence is that federal portion or federal money will go to the parent, so the parent can go to a tutoring program or another public school or another private school.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You see, there has to be a consequence.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a society that says hey, the status quo is fine, just move them through.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And guess who suffers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well, the program that he’s proposing is not the one that he just described.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Described under your plan, Governor Bush, states would be required to pay vouchers to students to match the vouchers so that the federal government would put up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, you’re — and the way it would happen is that under his plan, if a school was designated as failing, the kids would be trapped there for another three years and then some of them would get federal vouchers and the state would be forced to match those, that money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Under my plan, if a school is failing, we work with the states to give them the authority and the resources to close down that school and reopen it right away with a new principal, a new faculty, a turn-around team of specialists who know what they’re doing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s based on the plan of Governor Jim Hunt in North Carolina, and it works great.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If I thought that there was no alternative, then I might feel differently.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I have an obligation to fight to make sure there are no failing schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have to turn around — most schools are excellent, but we have to make sure that all of them are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: What grade do you teach?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: High school.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I mentioned before that the local communities are having a harder time passing bond issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Traditionally, if you’ve been involved in a campaign like that, you know that the parents with kids in school are the ones that turn out and vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s ironic that there are now — there is now a smaller percentage of the voters made up of parents with children than ever in American history because of the aging of our population, but at the same time we’ve got the largest generation of students in public schools ever.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: More than 90% of America’s children go to public schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And it’s the largest number ever this year and they’ll break the record next year and every year for ten years running.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to do something about this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And local — it’s not enough to leave it up to the local school districts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They’re not able to do it and our future depends upon it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Look, we’re in an information age.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Our economic future depends upon whether or not our children are going to get the kind of education that lets them go on to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And again, I want to make it possible for all middle-class families to send their kids to college and more Pell grants for those who are in the lower income groups also, and then I want to make sure that we have job training on top of that and lifelong learning, but it all starts with the public school teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: My proposal gives $10,000 hiring bonuses for those teachers who are — who get certified to teach in the areas where they’re most needed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, accountability, we basically agree on accountability.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: My plan requires testing of all students.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It also requires something that Governor Bush’s plan doesn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It requires testing of all new teachers, including in the subjects that they teach.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have to start treating teachers like the professionals that they are, and give them the respect and the kind of quality of life that will draw more people into teaching because we need a lot more teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When you total up all the federal spending he wants to do, it’s the largest increase in federal spending in years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And there’s just not going to be enough money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have been a governor of a big state, I have made education my number one priority.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what governors ought to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They ought to say this is the most important thing we do as a state.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The federal government puts about 6% of the money up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They put about, you know, 60% of the strings where you have to fill out the paperwork.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know if you have to be a paperwork filler-outer, but most of it’s because of the federal government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What I want to do is to send flexibility and authority to the local folks so you can choose what to do with the money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One size does not fit all.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I worry about federalizing education if I were you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe strongly that the federal government can help, we need to fund Headstart.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to have accountability.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Vice President’s plan does not have annual accountability, third grade, fourth grade, fifth grade.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to demand on results.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe strongly in a teacher protection act like I mentioned.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hear from teachers all the time about the lawsuits and the threats, respect in the classroom.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Part of it’s because you can’t — you can’t control the classroom.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t have a consequence for somebody without fear of getting sued under federal law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I’m going to ask the Congress to pass a teacher protection act.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I believe in flexibility, I believe in a national reading initiative for local districts to access with K through 2 diagnostic testing, curriculum that works, phonics works, by the way, it needs to be a part of our curriculum.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There needs to be flexibility for teacher training and teacher hiring with federal money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The federal government can be a part, but don’t fall prey to all this stuff about money here and money there because education is really funded at the local level.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 94% comes from the local level.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m so glad that I have the chance to knock that down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Look, the problem is that under Governor Bush’s plan, $1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: 6 trillion tax cut, mostly to the wealthy, under his own budget numbers, he proposes spending more money for a tax cut just for the wealthiest 1% than all the new money he budgets for education, health care and national defense combined.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now under my plan we’ll balance the budget every year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m not just saying this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m not just talking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I have helped to balance the budget for the first time in 30 years, paid down the debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And under my plan, in four years, as the percentage of our gross domestic product, federal spending will be the smallest that it has been in 50 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: One reason is, you know, the third biggest spending item in our budget is interest on the national debt?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We get nothing for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We keep the good faith and credit of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will pay down the debt every single year until it is eliminated early in the next decade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That gets rid of the third biggest intrusion of the federal government in our economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, because the governor has all this money for a tax cut mostly to the wealthy, there is no money left over, so schools get testing and lawsuit reform and not much else.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, he’s wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Just add up all the numbers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s three times bigger than what President Clinton proposed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Senate Budget Committee —

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That was in an ad, Jim, that was knocked down by the journalists who analyzed the ad and said it was misleading.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My turn?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Forget the journalists.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He proposed more than Walter Mondale and Michael Dukakis combined.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a big spender.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he ought to be proud of it, it’s part of his record.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We just have a different philosophy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me talk about tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you pay taxes, you ought to get tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Vice President believes only the right people ought to get tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think that’s the role of the president to pick you’re right and you’re not right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think if you’re going to have tax relief, everybody ought to get it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And therefore, wealthy people are going to get it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the top 1% will end up paying one-third of the taxes in America and they get one-fifth of the benefits.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s because we structured the plan so that six million additional American families pay no taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you’re a family of four making $50,000 in Missouri, you get a 50% cut in your federal income taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What I’ve done is set priorities and funded them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And there’s extra money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I believe the people who pay the bills ought to get some money back.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He wants to grow the government and I trust you with your own money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I wish we could spend an hour talking about trusting people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s just the right position to take.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Can we take the time —

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Of course it does.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you pay taxes, you are going to get a benefit.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: People who pay taxes will get tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me finish.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Under my plan, if you make — the top — the wealthy people pay 62% of the taxes today.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Afterwards they pay 64%.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a fair plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know why?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because the tax code is unfair for people at the bottom end of the economic ladder.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you’re a single mother making $22,000 a year today and you’re trying to raise two children, for every additional dollar you earn you pay a higher marginal rate on that dollar than someone making $200,000, and that’s not right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I want to do something about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Yeah, look.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Look, this isn’t about Governor Bush, it’s not about me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It is about you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I want to come back to something I said before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you want somebody who believes that we were better off eight years ago than we are now and that we ought to go back to the kind of policies that we had back then, emphasizing tax cuts mainly for the wealthy, here is your man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you want somebody who will fight for you and who will fight to have middle-class tax cuts, then I am your man.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, I doubt anybody here makes more than $330,000 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I won’t ask you, but if you do, you’re in the top 1%.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m not going to ask them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But if everyone here in this audience was dead on in the middle of the middle-class, then the tax cuts for every single one of you all added up would be less than the tax cut his plan would give to just one member of that top wealthiest 1%.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now you judge for yourselves whether or not that’s fair.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Good.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 50 million Americans get no tax relief under his plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That’s not right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You may not be one of them, you’re just not one of the right people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And secondly, we’ve had enough fighting.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time to unite.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You talk about eight years?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In eight years they haven’t gotten anything done on Medicare, on Social Security, a patient’s bill of rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time to get something done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Hey, I’ve got to answer that, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Medicare — I cast the tie-breaking vote to add 26 years to the life of Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It was due to go bankrupt in 1999 and that 50 million figure again, the newspapers — I said — you said forget the journalists, but they are the keepers of the score card and whether or not you’re using facts that aren’t right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And that fact is just not right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been a leader.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been a person who has to set a clear vision and convince people to follow.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got a strategy for the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And first let me say that our nation now needs to speak with one voice during this time, and I applaud the president for working hard to diffuse tensions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our nation needs to be credible and strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When we say we’re somebody’s friend, everybody has got to believe it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Israel is our friend and we’ll stand by Israel.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to reach out to moderate Arab nations as well to build coalitions to keep the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I also need — the next leader needs to be patient.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can’t put the Middle East peace process on our timetable.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s got to be on the timetable of the people that we’re trying to bring to the peace table.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can’t dictate the terms of peace, which means that you have to be steady.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t worry about polls or focus groups.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to have a clear vision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what a leader does.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A leader also understands that the United States must be strong to keep the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Saddam Hussein still is a threat in the Middle East.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Our coalition against Saddam is unraveling.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Sanctions are loosened.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The man who may be developing weapons of mass destruction, we don’t know because inspectors aren’t in.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So to answer your question, it requires a clear vision, a willingness to stand by our friends, and the credibility for people both friend and foe to understand when America says something, we mean it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I see a future when the world is at peace, with the United States of America promoting the values of democracy and human rights and freedom all around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Even in Iran they have had an election that began to bring about some change.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We stand for those values and we have to be willing to assert them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Right now our military is the strongest in the entire history of the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will — I pledge to you I will do whatever is necessary to make sure that it stays that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, what can I bring to that challenge?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: When I was a young man, my father was a senator opposed to the Vietnam War.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: When I graduated from college, there were plenty of fancy ways to get out of going and being a part of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I went and I volunteered, and I went to Vietnam.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t do the most or run the greatest risk by a long shot, but I learned what it was like to be an enlisted man in the United States Army.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: In the Congress, in the House of Representatives, I served on the House Intelligence Committee and I worked hard to learn the subject of nuclear arms control and how we can diffuse these tensions and deal with non-proliferation and deal with the problems of terrorism and these new weapons of mass destruction.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Look, we’re gonna face some serious new challenges in the next four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’ve worked on that long and hard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: When I went to the United States Senate, I asked for an assignment to the Armed Services Committee.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And while I was there I worked on a bipartisan basis, as I did in the House, I worked with former President Reagan on the modernization of our strategic weaponry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: In the Senate I was one of only ten Democrats, along with Senator Joe Lieberman, to support Governor Bush’s dad in the Persian Gulf War Resolution.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And for the last eight years I’ve served on the National Security Council.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Can I say just one other thing here?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Fine, I’ll wait.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think he gets a — oh, I’m sorry, you’re right, go ahead.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, sir.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Just to finish briefly, I started to say that for the last eight years I’ve been on the National Security Council.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Last week I broke up — I suspended campaigning for two days, or parts of two days, to go back and participate in the meetings that charted the President’s summit meeting that he just returned from earlier today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And our team of — our country’s team over there did a great job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s a difficult situation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The United States has to be strong in order to make sure that we can help promote peace and security and stability.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And that means keeping our military strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, I said earlier that we are the strongest military, but we need to continue improving readiness and making sure that our military personnel are adequately paid and that the combination of their pay and their benefits and their retirement as veterans is comparable to the stiff competition that’s coming in this strong economy from the private sector.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I have supported the largest pay raise in many a year, and I support another one now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I also support modernization of our strategic and tactical weaponry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The governor has proposed skipping a generation of technology.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that would be a mistake, because I think one of the ways we’ve been able to be so successful in Kosovo and Bosnia and Haiti and in other places is by having the technological edge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You know, we won that conflict in Kosovo without losing a single human life in combat, a single American life in combat.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, readiness.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The trends before we — before I got my current job were on the decline, the number of divisions were reduced.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I argued that we should reverse that trend and take it back up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I’m happy to tell you that we have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, in my budget for the next ten years I propose $100 billion for this purpose.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The governor proposes $45 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I propose more than twice as much because I think it’s needed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If this were a spending contest, I would come in second.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I readily admit I’m not going to grow the size of the federal government like he is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Your question was deployment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It must be in the national interests, must be in our vital interests whether we ever send troops.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The mission must be clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Soldiers must understand why we’re going.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The force must be strong enough so that the mission can be accomplished.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the exit strategy needs to be well-defined.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m concerned that we’re overdeployed around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: See, I think the mission has somewhat become fuzzy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Should I be fortunate enough to earn your confidence, the mission of the United States military will be to be prepared and ready to fight and win war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And therefore prevent war from happening in the first place.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There may be some moments when we use our troops as peacekeepers, but not often.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Vice President mentioned my view of long-term for the military.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure the equipment for our military is the best it can possibly be, of course.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we have an opportunity — we have an opportunity to use our research and development capacities, the great technology of the United States, to make our military lighter, harder to find, more lethal.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have an opportunity, really, if you think about it, if we’re smart and have got a strategic vision and a leader who understands strategic planning, to make sure that we change the terms of the battlefield of the future so we can keep the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a peaceful nation, and I intend to keep the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Spending money is one thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But spending money without a strategic plan can oftentimes be wasted.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: First thing I’m going to do is ask the Secretary of Defense to develop a plan so we are making sure we’re not spending our money on political projects, but on projects to make sure our soldiers are well-paid, well-housed, and have the best equipment in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, sir.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: MEMBER OF AUDIENCE: Would just like to know what is your opposition to the Brady Handgun bill?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m sorry, I didn’t hear that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: MEMBER OF AUDIENCE: Would like to know why you object to the Brady Handgun bill, if you do object to it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because in a recent TV ad it showed that the National Rifle Association says that if you are elected, that they will be working out of your office.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think the National Rifle Association ran that ad.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But let me just tell you my position on guns in general, sir, if you don’t mind.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: MEMBER OF AUDIENCE: That kind of bothers me when I see an ad like that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want you to explain that ad to me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I don’t think I ran the ad.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think somebody who doesn’t want me to be president might have run that ad.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That wasn’t my ad.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it might have been one of my opponent’s ads.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Here is what I believe, sir.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe law-abiding citizens ought to be allowed to protect themselves and their families.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe that we ought to keep guns out of the hands of people that shouldn’t have them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I’m for instant background checks at gun shows, I’m for trigger locks, I think that makes sense.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Matter of fact, we distributed free trigger locks in the State of Texas so that people can get them and put them on their guns to make their guns more safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to raise the age at which juveniles can have a gun.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I also believe strongly that we need to enforce laws on the books that the best way to make sure that we keep our society safe and secure is to hold people accountable for breaking the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If we catch somebody illegally selling a gun, there needs to be a consequence.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If we keep somebody — you know, illegally using a gun, there needs to be a consequence.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Enforcement of law, and the federal government can help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is a great program called Project Exile in Richmond, Virginia, where we focused federal taxpayers’ money and federal prosecutors and went after people who were illegally using guns.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: To me that’s how you make society the safest it can be.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so, yeah, sometimes I agree with some of these groups in Washington and sometimes I don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m a pretty independent thinker.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The one thing I’m for is a safe society.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m for enforcing laws on the books.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what is going to happen should I earn your confidence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well, it was not one of my ads, either, Governor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I am familiar with the statement, and it was made by one of the top-ranking officials of that organization.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you my position.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that some common sense gun safety measures are certainly needed with the flood of cheap handguns that have sometimes been working their way into the hands of the wrong people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But all of my proposals are focused on that problem, gun safety.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: None of my proposals would have any effect on hunters, or sportsmen, or people who use rifles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They’re aimed at the real problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Let’s make our schools safe, let’s make our neighborhoods safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Let’s have a three-day waiting period, cooling off, so we can have a background check to make sure that criminals and people who really shouldn’t have guns don’t get them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I would like to use my remaining time on this exchange, Jim, to respond to an exchange that took place just a moment ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because a couple of times the governor has said that I am for a bigger government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Governor, I’m not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And let me tell you what the record shows.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: For the last eight years I have had the challenge of running the streamlining program called Reinventing Government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And if there are any federal employees in this group, you know what that means.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The federal government has been reduced in size by more than 300,000 people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And it’s now the smallest number that we have had since the — the smallest in size since John Kennedy’s administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: During the last five years, Texas’s government has gone up in size.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Federal government has gone down, Texas’s government has gone up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, my plan for the future, I see a time when we have smaller, smarter government where you don’t have to wait in line because you can get services online cheaper, better, faster.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We can do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a bumper crop this year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But that’s the good news.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You know what the bad news is that follows on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The prices are low.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: In the last several years, the so-called Freedom To Farm Law has, in my view, been mostly a failure.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to change many of its provisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, many here who are not involved in farming don’t — won’t follow this, so just forgive me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because the 2% of the country that is involved in farming is important because the rest of us wouldn’t eat except for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And you guys have been having a hard time, and I want to fight for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to change those provisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I want to restore a meaningful safety net.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I think that you pointed the way in your comments, because when you say there are multiple things accomplished by farmers, you’re specifically including conservation and protection of the environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And yes, farmers are the first environmentalists.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And when they decide not to plow a field that is vulnerable to soil erosion, that may cost them a little money, but it helps the environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that we ought to have an expanded conservation reserve program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I think that the environmental benefits that come from sound management of the land ought to represent a new way for farmers to get some income that will enable them — enable you to make sensible choices in crop rotation, and when you leave the land fallow and the rest.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, I’ll go beyond that and say I think we need much more focus on rural economic development programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I see a time when the Internet-based activities are more available in the rural areas and where the extra source of income that farm families used to have from shoe factories is replaced by an extra source of income from working in the information economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: So we need to do a lot of things, but we ought to start with a better safety net.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would like our farmers feeding the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re the best producers in the world, and I want — I want the farmers feeding the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need to open up markets.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Exports are down, and every time an export number goes down, it hurts the farmer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want the next president to have fast track negotiating authority to open up markets around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Weâ€™re the best and the most efficient farmers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to use food as a diplomatic weapon from this point forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We shouldn’t be using food.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It hurts the farmers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not the right thing to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m for value-added processing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We need more work on value-added processing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You take the raw product you produce, I presume you’re a farmer, off your farm, and you convert it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Value-added processing is important.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m for research and development.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Spending research and development money so that we can use our technological base to figure out new uses for farm products.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m for getting rid of the death tax, completely getting rid of the death tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One reason family farmers are forced to sell early is because of the death tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is a bad tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The President shouldn’t have vetoed that bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a tax that taxes people twice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It penalizes the family farmer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So should I be fortunate enough to earn your vote, I also understand — I want to open up markets, but I also understand that farming is a part of our national security.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m from a big farm state.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re the second biggest state — farming state in the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I hear from my farmers and friends all the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Vice President is right, by the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Every day is earth day if you own the land.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I like the policies that will encourage farmers to put — set aside land as well for conservation purposes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Yeah.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m for a massive reform of the estate tax or the death tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And under the plan that I’ve proposed, 80% of all family farms will be completely exempt from the estate tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And the vast majority of all family businesses would be completely exempt, and all of the others would have sharply reduced.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: So 80% — now the problem with completely eliminating it goes back to the wealthiest 1%.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The amount of money that has to be raised in taxes for middle-class families to make up for completely eliminating that on the very wealthiest, the billionaires, that would be an extra heavy burden on middle-class families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And so let’s do it for most all, but not completely eliminate it for the very top.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Eliminating the death tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because people shouldn’t be taxed twice on their assets.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s either unfair for some or unfair for all.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Again, this is just a difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you’re from Washington, you want to pick and choose winners.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think that’s the role of the president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think if you’re going to have tax relief, everybody benefits.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, I think your plan — a lot of fine print in your plan, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President, with all due respect.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is — I’m not so sure 80% of the people get the death tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know this, 100% will get it if I’m the president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just don’t think it’s fair to tax people’s assets twice regardless of your status.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a fairness issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s an issue of principle, not politics.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Hi, Joyce.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: MEMBER OF AUDIENCE: Hi, Governor.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m very concerned about the morality of our country now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: TV, movies, the music that our children are, you know, barraged with every day.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I want to know if there’s anything that can be worked out with the — Hollywood, or whoever, to help get rid of some of this bad language and whatever, you know.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s just bringing the country down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And our children are very important to us and we’re concerned about their education at school.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We should be concerned about their education at home, also.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Appreciate that question.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Laura and I are proud parents of teenage girls, twin daughters, and I know what you’re saying.
