transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Government ought to stand on the side of parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Parents are teaching their children right from wrong, and the message oftentimes gets undermined by the popular culture.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You bet there’s things that government can do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can work with the entertainment industry to provide family hour.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can have filters on Internets where public money is spent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There ought to be filters in public libraries and filters in public schools so if kids get on the Internet, there is not going to be pornography or violence coming in.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to have character education in our schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know that doesn’t directly talk about Hollywood, but it does reinforce the values you’re teaching.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Greatly expand character education funding so that public schools will teach children values, values which have stood the test of time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s afterschool money available.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think that afterschool money ought to be available for faith-based programs and charitable programs that exist because somebody has heard the call to love a neighbor like you would like to be loved yourself.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That will help reinforce the values that parents teach at home as well.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Ours is a great land, and one of the reasons why is because we’re free.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I don’t support censorship.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I do believe that we ought to talk plainly to the Hollywood moguls and people who produce this stuff and explain the consequences.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we need to have rating systems that are clear.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I happen to like the idea of having technology for the TV, easy for parents to use so you can tune out these programs you don’t want in your house.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll remind mothers and dads the best weapon is the off/on button, and paying attention to your children, and eating dinner with them and being — I’m sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I was on my peroration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: My turn.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I care a lot about this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s not just movies; television, video games, music, the Internet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Parents now feel like you have to compete with the mass culture in order to raise your kids with the values that you want them to have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Tipper and I have four children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And God bless them, every one of them decided on their own to come here this evening.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to embarrass our oldest daughter.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: She and her husband made us grandparents almost a year-and-a-half ago, and yet if she’ll forgive me, when she was little, she brought a record home that had some awful lyrics in it and Tipper hit the ceiling.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And that launched a campaign to try to get the record companies to put ratings that — warning labels for parents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I’m so proud of what she accomplished in getting them on there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been involved myself in negotiating and helping to move along the negotiations with the Internet service providers to get a parents’ protection page every time 95% of the pages come up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And a feature that allows parents to automatically check with one click what sites your kids have visited lately.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You know, some parents are worried about those filters, that you will have to ask your kids how to put them on there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But if you can check up on them, that’s real power.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And recently the Federal Trade Commission pointed out that some of these entertainment companies have warned parents that the material is inappropriate for children, and then they’ve turned around behind the backs of the parents and advertised that same adult material directly to children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: That is an outrage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Joe Lieberman and I gave them six months to clean up their act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And if they don’t do it, we’re gonna ask for tougher authority in the hands of the FTC on the false and deceptive advertising.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’ll tell you this, I want to do something about this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Respect the First Amendment, but I will do something to help you raise your kids without that garbage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Right next to the last.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: MEMBER OF AUDIENCE: It seems that when we hear about issues of this campaign, it’s usually Medicare, Social Security or prescription drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: As a college professor, I hear a lot of apathy amongst young people who feel that there are no issues directed to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And they don’t plan to vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: How do you address that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to change it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I spend a good deal of time talking to young people, and in my standard speech out there on the stump I usually end my speech by saying, I want to ask you for something and I want to direct it especially to the young people in the audience.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I want to tell you what I tell them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Sometimes people who are very idealistic and have great dreams, as young people do, are apt to stay at arm’s length from the political process because they think their good hearts might be brittle, and if they invest their hopes and allow themselves to believe, then they’re gonna be let down and disappointed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But thank goodness we’ve always had enough people who have been willing in every generation to push past the fear of a broken heart and become deeply involved in forming a more perfect union.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We’re America, and we believe in our future and we know we have the ability to shape our future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, we’ve got to address one of the biggest threats to our democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And that is the current campaign financing system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I know they say it doesn’t rank anywhere on the polls.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe that’s a fair measure.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m telling you, I will make it the — I will make the McCain-Feingold Campaign Finance Reform bill the very first measure that I send to the Congress as president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Governor Bush opposes it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I wish that he would consider changing his mind on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because I think that the special interests have too much power, and we need to give our democracy back to the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you why.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Those issues you mentioned, Social Security, prescription drugs, the big drug companies are against the prescription drug proposal that I’ve made.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The HMOs are against the patient’s rights bill, the Dingle-Norwood bill that I support, and that Gov.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Bush does not support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The big oil companies are against the measures to get more energy independence and renewable fuel.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They ought to have their voices heard, but they shouldn’t have a big megaphone that drowns out the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We need campaign finance reform and we need to shoot straight with young and old alike and tell them what the real choices are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And we can renew and rekindle the American spirit and make our future what our founders dreamed it could be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We can.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Tell you what I hear.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A lot of people are sick and tired of the bitterness in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: and therefore they don’t want any part of politics.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They look at Washington and see people pointing fingers and casting blame and saying one thing and doing another.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s a lot of young folks saying, you know, why do I want to be involved with this mess?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And what I think needs to happen in order to encourage the young to become involved is to shoot straight, is to set aside the partisan differences, and set an agenda that will make sense.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Medicare, I know you talked about it, but Medicare is relevant for all of us, young and old alike.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We better get it right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Tax reform is relevant for old and young alike.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think it’s the issues that turn kids off.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s the tone.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s the attitude.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s a cynicism in Washington and it doesn’t have to be that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Before I decided to run, I had to resolve two issues in my mind.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One, could our family endure all this business.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I came to the conclusion that our love was strong enough to be able to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The other was could an administration change the tone in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I believe the answer is yes, otherwise I wouldn’t be asking for your vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what happened in Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We worked together.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is a man here in this audience named Hugo Berlanga.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He is the chairman of the health committee.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He came here for a reason, to tout our record on health in Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s a Democrat.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t care whether he was a Republican or Democrat.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What I cared about is could we work together.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: needs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And finally, sir, to answer your question, you need somebody in office who will tell the truth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s the best way to get people back in the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Hi, Norma.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: MEMBER OF AUDIENCE: Hi.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: How will your administration address diversity, inclusiveness, and what role will affirmative action play in your overall plan?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve had a record of bringing people from all walks of life into my administration, and my administration is better off for it in Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to find people that want to serve their country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I want a diverse administration, I think it’s important.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve worked hard in the State of Texas to make sure our institutions reflect the state with good, smart policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Policy that rejects quotas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t like quotas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Quotas tend to pit one group of people against another.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Quotas are bad for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not the way America is all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But policies that give people a helping hand so they can help themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For example, in our State of Texas I worked with the legislature, both Republicans and Democrats, to pass a law that said if you come in the top 10% of your high school class, you’re automatically admitted to one of our higher institutions of learning, college.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And as a result, our universities are now more diverse.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was a smart thing to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What I called it, I labeled it affirmative access.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the contracting business in government can help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Not with quotas, but help meet a goal of ownership of small businesses, for example.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The contracts need to be smaller, the agencies need to be — need to recruit and to work hard to find people to bid on the state contracts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we can do that in a way that represents what America is all about, which is equal opportunity and an opportunity for people to realize their potential.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So to answer your question, I support, I guess the way to put it, is affirmative access.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll have an administration that will make you proud.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I believe in this goal and effort with all my heart.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I believe that our future as a nation depends upon whether or not we can break down these barriers that have been used to pit group against group, and bring our people together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: How do you do it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well, you establish respect for differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You don’t ignore differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It’s all too easy for somebody in the majority in the population to say oh, we’re just all the same, without an understanding of the different life experience that you’ve had, that others have had.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Once you have that understanding and mutual respect, then we can transcend the differences and embrace the highest common denominator of the American spirit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know what affirmative access means.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I do know what affirmative action means.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I know the governor is against it, and I know that I’m for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I know what a hate crime statute pending at the national level is all about in the aftermath of James Byrd’s death.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m for that proposed law, the governor is against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I know what it means to have a commitment to diversity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I am part of an administration that has the finest record on diversity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And incidentally, an excellent — I mean, I think our success over the last eight years has not been in spite of diversity but because of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because we’re able to draw on the wisdom and experience from different parts of the society that hadn’t been tapped in the same way before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And incidentally, Mel Carnahan in Missouri had the finest record on diversity in any governor in the entire history of the State of Missouri.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I want to honor that among his other achievements here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, I just believe that what we have to do is enforce the civil rights laws.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m against quotas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: This is, with all due respect, Governor, that’s a red herring.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Affirmative action isn’t quotas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’m against quotas, they’re illegal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: They’re against the American way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Affirmative action means that you take extra steps to acknowledge the history of discrimination and injustice and prejudice and bring all people into the American dream because it helps everybody, not just those who are directly benefitting.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If affirmative action means quotas, I’m against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If affirmative action means what I just described what I’m for, then I’m for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You heard what I was for.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The vice president keeps saying I’m against things.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You heard what I was for, and that’s what I support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: He said if affirmative action means quotas, he’s against it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Affirmative action doesn’t mean quotas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Are you for it without quotas?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I may not be for your version, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President, but I’m for what I just described to the lady.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Are you for what the Supreme Court says is a constitutional way of having affirmative action?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that speaks for itself.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, it doesn’t speak for itself, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Vice President, it speaks for the fact that there are certain rules in this that we all agree to, but evidently rules don’t mean anything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you make less than $60,000 a year and you decide to invest $1,000 in a savings account, you’ll get a tax credit, which means in essence that the federal government will match your $1,000 with another $1,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you make less than $30,000 a year and you put $500 in a savings account, the federal government will match it with $1500.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you make more than $60,000 and up to 100 you’ll still get a match, but not as generous.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You’ll get an access to life-long learning and education, help with tuition if you want to get a new skill or training.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you want to purchase health insurance, you will get help with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you want to participate in some of the dynamic changes that are going on in our country, you will get specific help in doing that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you are part of the — of the bottom 20% or so of wage earners, then you will get an expanded earned income tax credit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now, the tax relief that I propose is directed specifically at middle-income individuals and families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And if you have a — if you have an elderly parent or grandparent who needs long-term care, then you will get help with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: $3,000 tax credit to help your expenses in taking care of a loved one who needs long-term care.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me just say the first — this business about the entitlement he tried to describe about savings, you know, matching savings here and matching savings there, fully-funded it’s gonna cost a whole lot of money, a lot more than we have.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’re going to get a tax relief in my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’re not going to be targeted in or targeted out.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Everybody that pays taxes is going to get tax relief.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you take care of an elderly in your home, you’re going to get the personal exemption increased.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think also what you need to think about is not the immediate, but what about Medicare?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You get a plan that will include prescription drugs, a plan that will give you options.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, I hope people understand that Medicare today is important, but it doesn’t keep up with the new medicines.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If you’re a Medicare person, on Medicare, you don’t get the new procedures.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’re stuck in a time warp in many ways.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So it will be a modern Medicare system that trusts you to make a variety of options for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’re going to live in a peaceful world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It will be a world of peace because we’re going to have a clear sight of foreign policy based upon a strong military and a mission that stands by our friends.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A mission that doesn’t try to be all things to all people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A judicious use of the military which will help keep the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’ll live in a world, hopefully, that is more educated so it’s less likely you’ll be harmed in your neighborhood.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: See, an educated child is one much more likely to be hopeful and optimistic.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’ll be in a world in which fits into my philosophy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The harder you work, the more you can keep.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s the American way.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Government shouldn’t be a heavy hand.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s what the federal government does to you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It should be a helping hand, and tax relief and the proposals I just described should be a good helping hand.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, I’m not proud of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The death penalty is a very serious business, Leo.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s an issue that good people obviously disagree on.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I take my job seriously.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if you think I was proud of it, I think you misread me, I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I was sworn to uphold the laws of my state.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: During the course of the campaign in 1994 I was asked do you support the death penalty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I said I did if administered fairly and justly.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because I believe it saves lives, Leo, I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If it’s administered swiftly, justly and fairly, it saves lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One of the things that happens when you’re a governor, at least oftentimes you have to make tough decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You can’t let public persuasion sway you, because the job is to enforce the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what I did, sir.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There have been some tough cases come across my desk.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Some of the hardest moments since I’ve been the governor of the State of Texas is to deal with those cases.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But my job is to ask two questions, sir.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Is the person guilty of the crime?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And did the person have full access to the courts of law?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I can tell you looking at you right now, in all cases those answers were affirmative.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m not proud of any record.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m proud of the fact that violent crime is down in the State of Texas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m proud of the fact that we hold people accountable.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I’m not proud of any record, sir, I’m not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I support the death penalty.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think that it has to be administered not only fairly with attention to things like DNA evidence, which I think should be used in all capital cases, but also with very careful attention.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If, for example, somebody confesses to the crime and somebody is waiting on death row, there has to be alertness to say wait a minute, have we got the wrong guy?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If the wrong guy is put to death, then that’s a double tragedy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Not only has an innocent person been executed, but the real perpetrator of the crime has not been held accountable for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And in some cases may be still at large.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But I support the death penalty in the most heinous cases.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s the only reason to be for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me finish, sir.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think you should support the death penalty to seek revenge.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think that’s right.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the reason to support the death penalty is because it saves other people’s lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think it is a deterrent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I know that’s a controversial view, but I do believe it’s a deterrent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I am a person who keeps promises.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, we’ve heard a lot about — from the governor about not much being done in the last eight years, as if the promises that I made eight years ago have not been kept.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I think the record shows otherwise.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have gone from the biggest deficits eight years ago to the biggest surpluses in history today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Instead of high unemployment, we now have the lowest African-American unemployment, the lowest Latino unemployment ever measured.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: 22 million new jobs, very low unemployment nationally.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Instead of ballooning the debt and multiplying it four times over, we have seen the debt actually begun to be paid down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Here are some promises that I’ll make to you now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will balance the budget every year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will pay down the debt every year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I will give middle-class Americans tax cuts, meaningful ones.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I will invest in education, health care, protecting the environment and retirement security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We both made promises in this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I promise you I will keep mine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Let me tell you about one of the governor’s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: He has promised a trillion dollars out of the Social Security Trust Fund for young working adults to invest and save on their own.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: But he’s promised seniors that their Social Security benefits will not be cut, and he’s promised the same trillion dollars to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: So this is a show me state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Reminds me of the line from the movie, “Show me the money.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: ” Which one of those promises will you keep and which will you break, Governor?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you for your question.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I — there’s an old high school debating trick, which is to answer something and then attack your opponent at the end.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You asked about promises.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You were promised that Medicare would be reformed, and that Social Security would be reformed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You were promised a middle-class tax cut in 1992.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It didn’t happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s too much bitterness in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s too much wrangling.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s time to have a fresh start.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One of the reasons I was successful as the governor of Texas is because I didn’t try to be all things to all people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When I campaigned in a race, a lot of folks didn’t think I could win including, by the way, my mother.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I said I’d do four things; tort reform, education reform, welfare reform and juvenile justice reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I won.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I had the will of the people in my state behind me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then I brought folks together to get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s what we need, I think, in this election.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: To me that’s what it’s all about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m sure your 6th grade kids are listening and saying, these guys will say anything to get elected.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But there’s a record, and that’s what I hope people look at.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One of my promises is going to be Social Security reform, and you bet, we need to take a trillion dollars out of that $2.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: 4 trillion surplus.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now remember, Social Security revenue exceeds expenses up until 2015.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: People are going to get paid.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But if you’re a younger worker, if you’re younger, you better hope this country thinks differently, otherwise you’re gonna be faced with huge payroll taxes or reduced benefits.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And you bet we’re gonna take a trillion dollars of your own money and let you invest it under safe guidelines so you get a better rate of return on the money than the paltry 2% that the federal government gets for you today.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s one of my promises.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it’s gonna require people to bring both Republicans and Democrats together to get it done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s what it requires.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There was a chance to get this done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was a bipartisan approach, but it’s been rejected.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to bring them together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, Jim, I would like to respond to what the governor just said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Because the trillion dollars that has been promised to young people has also been promised to older people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And you cannot keep both promises.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you’re in your mid-40’s under the governor’s plan, Social Security will be bankrupt by the time you retire, if he takes it out of the Social Security Trust Fund.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Under my plan it will be — its solvency will be extended until you’re 100.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now that is the difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And the governor may not want to answer that question, he may want to call it a high school debating trick, but let me tell you this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: This election is not about debating tricks, it is about your future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: The reason Social Security — he says it gets 2%.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You know, it’s not a bank account that just pays back money that’s invested.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: It is also used to give your mothers and fathers the Social Security checks that they live on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you take a trillion dollars out of that Social Security Trust Fund, how are the checks going to be — how are you going to keep faith with the seniors?

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Now let me come directly to your question.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, can I answer that?

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One reason people are skeptical is because people don’t answer the questions they’ve been asked.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The trillion dollars comes out of the surplus so that you can invest some of your own money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There’s just a difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want workers to have their own assets.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s who you trust, government or people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much, Jim, and I’ll begin by answering your questions — your last question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I believe that a lot of people are skeptical about people in politics today because we have seen a time of great challenge for our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Since the assassination of our best leaders in the ’60’s, since the Vietnam War, since Watergate, and because we need campaign finance reform.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I would like to tell you something about me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I keep my word.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I have kept the faith.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I’ve kept the faith with my country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I volunteered for the Army.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I served in Vietnam.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I kept the faith with my family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Tipper and I have been married for 30 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have devoted ourselves to our children and now our nearly one-and-a-half-year-old grandson.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I have kept the faith with our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Nine times I have raised my hand to take an oath to the Constitution, and I have never violated that oath.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I have not spent the last quarter century in pursuit of personal wealth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I have spent the last quarter century fighting for middle-class working men and women in the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: I believe very deeply that you have to be willing to stand up and fight no matter what powerful forces might be on the other side.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: If you want somebody who is willing to fight for you, I am asking for your support and your vote and, yes, your confidence and your willingness to believe that we can do the right thing in America, and be the better for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We’ve made some progress during the last eight years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: We have seen the strongest economy in the history of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Lower crime rates for eight years in a row.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: Highest private home ownership ever, but I’ll make you one promise here.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: You ain’t seen nothing yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Al Gore
transcript_turns.text: And I will keep that promise.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, Jim, I want to thank you and thank the folks here at Washington University and the vice president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Appreciate the chance to have a good, honest dialogue about our differences of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think after three debates the good people of this country understand there is a difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is a difference between big federal government and somebody who is coming from outside of Washington who will trust individuals.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got an agenda that I want to get done for the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s an agenda that says we’re going to reform Medicare to make sure seniors have got prescription drugs and to give seniors different options from which they can choose.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s an agenda that says we’re listen to the young voices in Social Security and say we’re going to think differently about making sure we have a system, but also fulfill the promise to the seniors in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A promise made will be a promise kept should I be fortunate enough to become your president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to have the military keeping the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to make sure the public school system in America keeps its promise so not one child is left behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: After setting priorities, I want to give some of your money back.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think the surplus is the government’s money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s the people’s money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think the surplus exists because of the ingenuity and hard work of the federal government, I think it exists because of the ingenuity and hard work of the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And you ought to have some of this surplus so you can save and dream and build.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I look forward to the final weeks of this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m asking for your vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For those of you for me, thanks for your help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For those of you for my opponent, please only vote once.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But for those who have not made up their mind, I would like to conclude by this promise.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Should I be fortunate enough to become your president, when I put my hand on the Bible, I will swear to not only uphold the laws of the land, but I will also swear to uphold the honor and the dignity of the office to which I have been elected, so help me God.

transcript_turns.speaker: George W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much.
